The encomium placed in the calendar entry is taken from Ado [Col. 0989A]; as we said on the preceding day, our author excerpted his material from the most authentic Acts. It remains to add here Wandalbert’s eulogy:

*James and Marianus, having obtained equal honor of martyrdom,  
Meet their destined end on the day before the Kalends of April.*

The following Euprobus—or rather Eutropes, or Eutropius—was taken from Gregory of Tours and recorded by Ado; his eulogy Our Author also transcribed from the aforementioned Ado, without investigating the matter at all, as is his custom, and adhering to the tradition then received concerning the first bishops sent into Gaul by Saint Clement. Gregory of Tours, however, had narrated this only with the word “it is said,” as Henschenius carefully observes. From this you will easily understand that the opinion of many modern scholars is correct: they admit nothing concerning Eutropius that is certain in every respect, apart from his cult and relics, about which the aforementioned Gregory speaks somewhat more confidently. See what is reported at length in the Acts concerning his miracles. Up to this point, then, the text is the genuine text of Usuard.

[Col. 0990A] Ado continues: “In Asia, the passion of Saint Maximus, martyr, whose deeds are preserved.” In our Acts another Greek of the same name is indeed added. But whether that Asiatic Maximus truly belongs to Ado is made doubtful by Mosander’s edition, in which Quirinus and Sophia are also added; these are without doubt to be counted among the additions. Why, then, should the aforementioned Maximus not also have been omitted by Notker, otherwise a careful copyist of Ado? Florus mentions Maximus and Quirinus. As for the latter, the Vigil of the Apostles is additionally recorded in the Romanum parvum, very probably added by some later hand, just as Quirinus probably slipped into that manuscript, once kept at Cologne, on the occasion of the translation to Neuss. See our Acts for 30 March, where you will find discussed what concerns the true title of Quirinus. Ruinartius again extracted the Acts of the Asiatic Maximus from our Acts as genuine and prefixed an erudite notice, beginning on page 143.]

[Note: [Col. 0989B]

HERINIEN. As is customary, it inserts the proper material of the province of Rheims, writing in second place as follows: “On the same day, the birthday of Saint Madernianus, archbishop of Rheims, who was the sixth to govern that same church.” In the Acts the name is Maternianus. The manuscripts, however, pronounce it differently.

TORNACEN. The text seems to fit the material into its own brackets rather than to fit the brackets to the material. It would be extremely pure if it did not omit what follows after *supplicia* up to *cum multis*.

PULSANEN. It is more mutilated, since the entire eulogy of Marianus and Jacobus has been cut away. At the end, however, after *victor*, it writes: “And as a martyr he departed to the Lord.”

ROSWEYD. At the end: “Likewise at Alexandria, of Pastor, bishop, with twenty-four others burned by fire and cast into the sea.” See the entire series in the Acts.

ANTUERP.-MAJ. Also at the end: “At London, [Col. 0989C] the deposition of Saint Erchenwald, bishop and confessor.” You will find the name written in various forms.

CENTULEN.: “The birthday of the holy Marianus and Jacobus, who were burned with many others under Dacian. At Sanctonas, of Saint Eutropius, bishop and martyr. In Asia, of Saint Maximus, martyr, whose deeds are preserved.”

BRUXELLEN. In first place it treats Eutropius, and in second the Lambesian martyrs, quite purely. It follows with Maximus, as above. Then: “At Jerusalem, of Quiriacus, also called Judas, who found the cross of Christ, and whom Queen Helena, after he had been baptized, had ordained bishop of Jerusalem; and who afterward, under the emperor Julian the Apostate, suffered a celebrated martyrdom for the faith of Christ.” He is referred to the following day and to 4 May. “At Rome, on the Appian Way, the elevation of Saint Quirinus, martyr, whose passion is celebrated on the third day before the Kalends of April. And the deposition of Saint Erembert, bishop.”

[Col. 0989D] HAGENOYEN. After the pure text he adds: “On the same day, the translation of Saint Quirinus, soldier and tribune, on which day his sacred relics were carried from Rome to the city of Neuss by the bishop of Cologne, and from there his shrine is still deposited on that same day and carried around on the following day. At the city of Auch, Saint Orientius, bishop and confessor, who, adorned with every virtue, is said to have rested in peace by a holy death.” See the following day. “At Brescia, blessed Maxentia, widow.” Below she is said to have been the mother of Vigilius.

AQUICINCT. At the end: “And Saint Erembert, bishop.” He is venerated on 4 May. “In Britain, in the city of London, Saint Erconpald,” etc., as MOLANUS has it in the later editions. But instead of *veritatis*, the manuscript wrongly reads *vere viriditatis*.

MATRIC.-CARTH.-ULTRAJ.: “Of Quirinus, martyr. Of Eutropius, bishop and martyr. Of Jacobus, martyr, and Marianus, lector, martyred with many others. Of Madernianus, archbishop of Rheims, sixth in succession.”

VATICAN. no. 5949: “At Alexandria, of the holy [Col. 0990A] Dorotheus, priest; Pomodianus and Rodocianus, deacons, who were burned by fire and cast into the sea with twenty-four others. In Asia, of Saint Maximus, martyr.” See what has been said in the Observations.

ALTEMPS.: “In Saxony, Oswald, bishop and confessor, whom Bede mentions in his history of the English.” He was treated on 28 February. “Likewise, Saint Cyrinus, martyr.” Other witnesses have “Quirinus. In Asia, Saint Maximus, martyr, whose deeds are preserved.”

FLORENTIN. In first place: “At Neuss, in the province of Cologne, of the holy martyrs Quirinus with his twelve companions. Likewise, of Saint Maxentia, widow, mother of Saint Vigilius.”

SALINEN. Of Saint Anatolius: “In the territory of Besançon, the translation of the body of Saint Eustasius, abbot of Luxeuil.” See 29 March.

[Col. 0990C] CABILLONEN. Of Saint Vincent: “Of Saint Flavius. And at the city of Chalon, the birthday of the most blessed Desideratus, priest and confessor, who was of eminent conversion [or, perhaps, conduct?] and miracles, in the monastery of Gourdon, where he also died. Blessed Agricola, bishop of that same place, buried him in the basilica of blessed Martin, which is in the suburb of the aforesaid city; there, through the healings obtained, the sick experience what merit he has with God.” In the Acts, Flavius too is called bishop of Chalon.

The LUBECK-COLOGNE edition begins: “At Neuss, on the bank of the Rhine, in the territory of Cologne, the translation of Saint Quirinus, tribune and martyr. His venerable body was requested from the supreme pontiff by the noble and religious Lady Gepa, abbess; she transferred it from Rome to her own city of Neuss and honorably placed it in her monastery.” A fairly pure text follows. Then: “In England, in the city of London, the birthday of Saint Erkenwald, bishop and confessor of that place. In Asia, the passion of Saint Maximus, martyr, whose deeds [Col. 0990D] are preserved.”

GREVEN.: “In Asia, according to Ado, the passion of Saint Maximus, martyr, whose deeds are preserved. In Alexandria, of Euphrodisius, priest and martyr, and thirty others. Likewise, of the holy Dorotheus, Crispinus, and Pomodianus. Of Euticia, martyr, under Licinius. At Rome, of Quirinus, bishop. Of Erconwald, bishop of London and confessor. Concerning him Bede says in Book IV: ‘The life and conduct of this man, both in his episcopate and before his episcopate, are said to have been most holy, just as even now the signs of heavenly virtues bear witness.’ Of Madernianus, archbishop of Rheims and confessor. On the same day, Saint Laurentius, priest of Novara. At Sanctonas, Saint Eustella, virgin, daughter of the king, converted by Eutropius.” See the index of the saints omitted from the proper days. “In England, Tybba, virgin.” Concerning her, see the Acts for 6 March. “Likewise, Maxentia, a most noble woman, mother of Saint Vigilius, bishop of Trent. In the diocese of Cologne, at the town of Neuss, the translation,” etc., almost as above. “Likewise, [Col. 0991A] in the diocese of Lyon, Saint Margaret, virgin, of the Carthusian Order. Once, when she was attending the office of Mass and ardently desired to partake of the sacred mysteries, suddenly the most merciful Bridegroom, our Lord Jesus Christ, who was accustomed frequently to visit and console her, transferred a portion of the host of his life-giving body from the priest’s hands into the mouth of his beloved bride. At last, full of good works, she rested in peace.” In the Acts she is listed among the saints omitted from the proper days.

MOLAN.: “At Rome, Saint Quirinus, tribune, etc.,” word for word as Ado has it on 30 March. Then he adds: “Although the passion of this beloved and precious martyr of God occurred on 29 March, it is nevertheless celebrated festively here, [Col. 0992A] because on this day the sacred relics of his body were transferred from the city of Rome to the city of Neuss above the Rhine. On the same day, the birthday of Saint Madernianus, etc.,” exactly as in HERINIEN. Concerning Maximus, Laurentius, and Erconwald, as in GREVEN above. In other editions: “At Rome, Saint Quirinus, tribune and martyr. Of this beloved one of God, etc. In Britain, in the city of London, Saint Erconwald, bishop and confessor. While he was still living an active life, loving the contemplative life with all his strength, he showed the peoples entrusted to him the path of truth by words and examples; adorned with many virtues, he departed to Christ.” Concerning Madernianus, Maximus, and Laurentius, as above.]

[Col. 0987]

At the city of Lambesis, the birthday of the holy martyrs Marianus, lector, and Jacobus, deacon. The former, after he had long before overcome in the confession of Christ the assault of the persecution of Decius, was seized again with his most beloved companion. Then, after dreadful and elaborate tortures, they were wonderfully strengthened and encouraged a second time by divine revelations; finally, they were put to death by the sword with many others. At the city of Sanctonas, blessed Euprobus, martyr, whom Saint Clement, having consecrated him by the dignity of the pontifical order, is said to have sent into Gaul; and, after completing his preaching, he fell victoriously for the testimony of Christ, his head having been dashed against something.
